description: Prism uses AI-assisted development but keeps generated-slop signals on whole-repo visibility so existing lowerer clone debt remains visible while stricter duplication, complexity, generic bloat, and unfinished-stub weights apply.

evidence.summary: Assume AI assistance is present and tighten the places where generative output most often drifts: duplication, complexity, generic bloat, and unfinished stubs. Best for teams that want AI-assisted mode to be explicit, visible in the vector, and enforced through normal preset mechanics rather than a hidden switch.

provenance.summary: Removed modes.ai_assisted so generated-slop scoring remains whole-repo instead of changed-hunk-only; existing lowerer clone debt is legitimate Prism compiler debt rather than calibration noise.

evidence.summary: With modes.ai_assisted active, generated-slop reported 1.000 because TS-SL-01 and TS-SL-02 analyzed only changed hunks; built-in/default whole-repo runs identified real lowerer duplication.

provenance.summary: Deferred baseline and project-module activation intentionally: current hard gates pass without a baseline, and the suggested Effect project module needs package availability review before becoming repo policy.

evidence.summary: pulsar calibrate suggest reports baseline.set and @skastr0/pulsar-project-module-effect as remaining suggestions; neither is required for this repo-local vector, conventions, and glossary calibration.
